blocks.text:
A sightseeing tour of high-altitude La Paz takes about 4 hours. It includes historic landmarks and the famous Witches’ Market. The city sprawls across the mountains, so even short drives open up views of the Andes and the densely built-up hillsides.

Then continue to the Valley of the Moon. Water and wind have shaped the salt, sand and rock into pointed crags, towers and deep furrows. Towards sunset, the slopes take on shades of gold and red. Overnight at the hotel.
The lights of La Paz at night against dark slopes and snow-covered mountains, Bolivia
La Paz at night: city lights below a snowy peak

Transfer from the hotel to the airport for the flight to Uyuni, which takes about 50 minutes. This is where the expedition part of your journey begins.

First, stop at the Train Cemetery. Then travel to Colchani, a salt-processing centre, to learn how salt is dried, ground and packaged. From there, the vehicle heads out onto the salt flat. Along the way, stop at Ojos de Salar, where you can see activity beneath the salt crust, and then at Playa Blanca, the first salt hotel and museum.

Around midday, you’ll reach Incahuasi Island. Limestone rocks and large cacti rise from the white expanse. There are caves and tunnels, and the high ground gives you a panoramic view of the salt flat in all directions.

The route then crosses Uyuni from north to south and follows a chain of snow-covered volcanoes in Lípez, with Ollagüe Volcano visible in the distance. Next, enter the Eduardo Avaroa National Reserve, where wild vicuñas live. The day ends at Lakes Cañapa, Hedionda and Honda, where you may see three flamingo species typical of the Andes. Overnight at an expedition lodge.
